title: Bounding Kirkwood-Dirac negativity of Gaussian processes
authors: Luca Bianchi, Carlo Marconi, Riccardo Cioli, Jan Sperling
abstract: The Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability provides an operational representation of a quantum state, whose negativity serves as a measure of nonclassicality. Despite its fundamental importance, the extremal values of the Kirkwood-Dirac negativity are still unknown in the general case. We investigate the Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability of an arbitrary quantum state under Gaussian processes. In this setting, we derive an upper bound on the negativity for any number of modes and measurements. For a single mode and two measurements, we show that the eigenstates of the quadrature operators saturate this upper bound, while a nontrivial minimum is reached by pure Gaussian states. As a consequence, our results indicate that Gaussian states are sufficient to achieve extreme values of nonclassicality.
summary: This paper develops an upper bound for the Kirkwood-Dirac negativity, a measure of nonclassicality in continuous variable quantum systems subjected to Gaussian processes. Through advanced mathematical techniques involving phase-space representations and Lorentz invariance, the authors prove that these extreme values can be reached using only Gaussian states. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for characterizing nonclassical resources.
main_problem: The primary goal is to derive an upper bound for the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD) negativity, a measure of nonclassicality, when applied to quantum states undergoing Gaussian processes.
main_result: The authors establish that Gaussian states are sufficient to achieve the extreme values (both maximum and minimum) of the KD negativity in the analyzed regimes. They derive explicit formulas for these bounds based on covariance matrices.
method: The analysis heavily relies on mapping quantum operators to phase-space functions using the Weyl representation, employing techniques from symplectic geometry and Lorentz invariance to simplify the calculation of determinants involving covariance matrices.
model_or_system: The system under study is continuous-variable (CV) quantum systems described by an M-mode state undergoing N sequential measurements $\{\hat{\Pi}_i\}$ governed by Gaussian dynamics. The focus is on characterizing nonclassicality via the KD quasiprobability $Q(\mathbf{r})$.
key_observables: KD Negativity ($\mathcal{N}$ or $\mathcal{N}_g$), which quantifies nonclassicality; the covariance matrix ($\sigma$).
important_parameters: Number of modes ($M$), number of measurements ($N$), squeezing parameters, and Lorentz invariants derived from the state's covariance structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes Gaussian dynamics and measurements for deriving the primary bounds. Later parts utilize specific coordinate transformations (e.g., Center-of-Mass frame) to simplify optimization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate 2D slices of the KD quasiprobability $Q(r)$ for various states (Fock, cat), comparing calculated negativity against theoretical maximums and minimums across varying state parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem and deriving a general upper bound based on covariance matrices. It then specializes to Gaussian input states, derives closed-form expressions for negativity, and finally uses advanced mathematical techniques (Lorentz invariance, Loewner monotonicity) to prove that Gaussian states saturate these bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify nonclassicality in CV systems using phase-space methods. The finding that Gaussian states suffice for extremal values is a significant theoretical result applicable across quantum optics and measurement theory.
